Subject: Tenant residency confirmation & private endpoint charter

Hi Soojin / Marissa —

Thanks for taking this on. As part of our security review we need explicit confirmation of the following before we can submit the SIG/CAIQ to Security: 

- Can Redwood host MedAlign data and inference for our account entirely within the EU (eu-west-1) for both storage and processing?
- For the private deployment option, what is the expected architecture for the private endpoint / peering? We need to confirm that egress stays within the EU and that keys can be partitioned by customer.
- Are there any SOC 2 artifacts or CAIQ responses you can share while we complete procurement?

We are happy to sign an NDA if needed. If you can provide a short attestation + diagram and a checklist of artifacts, we can get this into our legal/security queue.

Morning all —

Couple of technical clarifications that should help your infra team: 

- Architecture: For Private Deployment we deploy a customer-dedicated tenant in our EU region (eu-west-1). Connectivity options: (A) Customer-managed peering (VPC peering or PrivateLink) where the customer owns the VPC and controls routing; (B) Redwood-hosted VPC with a customer-dedicated subnet and private-peering to customer network (less common for regulated customers).

- Egress & data locality: By default all ephemeral compute, model weights, KV caches, and logs for the tenant are pinned to the eu-west-1 region; we implement network egress controls and route tables to prevent accidental cross-region access. Backups and audit logs are also kept in-region unless you request replication.

- KMS/keys: We support customer-managed keys in a separate KMS partition for Private Deployments. That partition and operator access can be scoped so Redwood operators cannot decrypt customer data without explicit key release procedures (we document key rotation and access governance in the runbook).

- Attachments: privatelink-architecture-diagram.png attached (simple view showing peering options + routing).

If you want, we can also provide a short runbook excerpt that lists the IAM roles/approvals used for operator access and the audit-forwarding endpoints for your SIEM.

Cheers,
Jonas Weber
Senior Infra Engineer — Private Deployments
jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com

Oliver —

Attached please find: 
- redwood_eu_residency_attestation_v1.pdf (formal attestation stating that MedAlign's tenant will be hosted in eu-west-1 under Redwood Private Deployment; includes statement on retention and in-region audit logs),
- CAIQ-responses-medalign.xlsx (filtered CAIQ answers relevant to data residency and network controls).

Summary (short):
- Residency: Redwood will provision your tenant in eu-west-1; all processing, transient caches, backups and audit logs for the tenant are retained in-region by default.
- Private connectivity: We recommend customer-managed VPC peering or AWS PrivateLink into the customer VPC. The peering approach leaves routing and egress control to MedAlign; our diagrams show both options.
- KMS: We support customer-managed KMS keys scoped to your tenant and a documented operator access workflow; keys reside in the EU KMS region.
- SOC 2 / artifacts: SOC 2 Type II summary is available in our Dataroom link (see related_links). Full SOC artifacts are on a need-to-know basis and can be provided under your NDA / dataproc agreements.

Next steps: If this looks good, Marissa and I can schedule a 30-minute review with your infra team next Tuesday (09:00–12:00 UTC available). If procurement needs any additional language for the SOW, please flag the exact clause and we will respond.

Thanks —
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com
